Office Visit - Follow-up
Patient: Cyrus Vasquez | DOB: 11/17/1967 | MRN: SYN-7286686
Date of service: 11/10/2025 | Dr. Kaveh Kestrel, MD

History of present illness:
57-year-old man seen for follow-up of low back pain. Low back pain radiating to the left leg for 14 weeks.

Treatment to date:
Completed 6 weeks of physical therapy and daily naproxen without adequate relief.

History:
Past medical history: gastroesophageal reflux, hypertension.
Medications: omeprazole 20 mg daily; lisinopril 10 mg daily.

Review of systems:
Red flag screen negative: denies bowel or bladder dysfunction, saddle anesthesia, fever, unexplained weight loss, or history of cancer.

Physical exam:
Back: tenderness over the lower lumbar paraspinal muscles; straight-leg raise positive on the left at 45 degrees.
Neuro: strength 4/5 in left plantar flexion, left Achilles reflex 1+, decreased light touch over the lateral left foot.

Assessment and plan:
Assessment: left S1 lumbar radiculopathy.
Plan: MRI lumbar spine without contrast to evaluate for disc herniation; home exercise program; follow up after imaging.
